title: Tensor coherence of the normalized scalar extension maps
statement: For any simultaneous normalized scalar and tensor-Hom models M [def-sfb-scalar-hom-comparison-data] and any family mu_a of ScalarHomTensorComparison, the two tensor routes for a:R→S and b:S→T agree: F_b(mu_a) followed by mu_b and tensor of the unit-normalized scalarHomExtensionComp maps equals scalarHomExtensionComp at the tensor followed by mu_(ab). For the identity ring map, tensor of scalarHomExtensionId inverse equals that inverse at the tensor followed by mu_id. These are equalities of actual derived tensor morphisms, without internal Hom or any flatness assumption. The full equations are the Lean attachment.

proof.text: Use the unit equation for leftAdjointUniq to identify the ordinary composition and identity comparisons. Map these comparisons termwise to complexes. Test the chain composition and identity squares after the ordinary scalar adjunction on every total pure generator. Naturality of the ordinary unit, the specified generators equations, and the unit equations for the ordinary comparisons give equality. Pure-tensor generation, followed by coproduct generation, proves equality of the chain maps.

proof.text: The scalar-pair normalization first gives the unit square on K-flat complexes with flat terms. For any complex choose its K-flat resolution with flat terms. Naturality of the derived unit, the universal comparison and the exact restriction comparison transfers the unit square along this resolution; cancel its localized quasi-isomorphism. The unit square determines every normalized transpose. Apply these transpose equations and the canonical exact restriction composition and identity equations to identify the derived left-adjoint comparison on all complexes with the ordinary chain comparison.

proof.text: On K-flat pairs, paste the three tensor-normalization squares with the just-proved scalar-comparison square and chain tensor coherence. Cancel the source tensor model isomorphism and the invertible scalar-pair comparisons on each factor. Naturality of the tensor model comparisons supplies the final transport. The same argument for the identity gives its hom equation, and inversion gives the stated inverse equation. Every derived object is isomorphic to the localization of a complex, which has a K-flat resolution. The localized resolving quasi-isomorphism gives a K-flat representative of that object. Naturality transports equality of the two natural transformations from K-flat representative pairs to every pair of derived objects.
